findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The bar hand washing sink was obstructed by the garbage can. CORRECTED- the can was moved. Find a new placement for the trash can that does not block the sink. Hand washing sinks must be maintained accessible at all times to allow for hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the baffles of the ice machine to contain an accumulation of soil debris. CORRECTED- The ice was covered, and baffles were cleaned and sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent contamination of consumables.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed the handle of the double door standing freezer upstairs to be in disrepair. The current handle is corner trim and duct tape. Duct tape is an adhesive, and therefore deteriorates. Discussed applying a sheet metal with a convex handle. CORRECTED- the duct tape was removed.  All nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed chemical sanitizing dish machine to be dispensing 0 ppm Cl. CORRECTED- the dish machine was primed and re-run until 50 ppm Cl was observed. Ensure frequent testing of sanitizer concentration with test strips to ensure proper sanitation of food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the handle of the double door standing freezer upstairs to be in disrepair. The handle had been broken off and replaced with a pool noodle and scotch tape. The PIC stated that they are working on ordering a replacement part. Ensure equipment is maintained in repair. All nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple items within the physical facility in need of repair. 
1) The floor drain cover in front of the dish machine is missing.
2) Caulking behind the triple sink is fragmented. 
Ensure these items are replaced and resealed by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
All three Allergen certificates on file were observed to have expired last year. High risk establishments are required to have Allergen training for their Certified Food Protection Managers. Ensure managers retake the Allergen course by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed 3 soup ladles hanging in ready to use position behind cheese sauce hot holding in kitchen to contain soil accumulation. CORRECTED- ladles were taken to the triple sink to be cleaned and sanitized before use. Ensure utensils that are stored in ready to use position are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning. [P]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a contained of white powder (identified as flour) above the pizza station at the end of the kitchen. CORRECTED-person in charge was notified and the flour was voluntarily discarded. Ensure white powders and other items that can be mistaken for others are labeled after they are removed from their original container.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a 2 oz. plastic container submerged in flour being stored on the shelf above the pizza station. CORRECTED- person in charge discarded the contents of the entire container (see violation #37). Use scoops with handles directed outwards, outside of the food to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the handle of the double door standing cooler upstairs to be in disrepair. The handle had been broken off and replaced with a pool noodle and scotch tape. Inspector notified the person in charge so that the equipment can be repaired. Ensure equipment is maintained in repair.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- Inspector observed soil accumulation along the gasket perimeter of the chest freezers upstairs. CORRECTED- the person in charge wiped the gaskets with a clean sanitizer rag. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple items in the facility in need of physical repair;
1) There is a hole in the ceiling upstairs above the soda boxes. This may be indicative of water damage. The inspector notified the person in charge of this damage, so that it may be repaired by the next routine inspection.
2) The mop sink at the entry of the kitchen was observed to have degraded caulking between the sink and the wall. The area between the mop sink basin and wall should be cleaned and either repaired or replaced.
Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good condition.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Buttermilk observed in the cook-line prep cooler was out of date per the manufacturer’s label. PIC was informed and the buttermilk was voluntarily discarded. Ensure staff discarding any out of date items.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Shell eggs were observed to be stored in a prep cooler below raw beef slider patties. Raw eggs should be stored above raw ground meat, but below fresh produce and other ready-to-eat foods. PIC was informed of incorrect storage, and eggs were moved to the walk-in cooler. Violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Fourteen bottles of Simply brand orange juice were observed stored on an ambient shelf in dry storage. The bottles are marked “keep refrigerated,” and the Coca-Cola website states that the Simply branded juices contain no preservatives, and therefore require refrigeration at all times. Juices were discarded. Violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Peeled hard-boiled eggs were observed stored in water in both the prep cooler and walk-in cooler. Storing eggs in water presents an unnecessary risk of cross-contamination. PIC was informed that eggs should be kept in a food-safe container free of ice or water.
findings.citation_text: 3-303.12 Storage or Display of Food in Contact with Water or Ice. (A) PACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with ice or water if the FOOD is subject to the entry of water because of the nature of its packaging, wrapping, or container or its positioning in the ice or water (B) Except as specified in (C) and (D) of this section, unPACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with undrained ice. (C) Whole, raw fruits or vegetables; cut, raw vegetables such as celery or carrot sticks or cut potatoes; and tofu may be immersed in ice or water. (D) Raw poultry and raw FISH that are received immersed in ice in shipping containers may remain in that condition while in storage awaiting preparation, display, service, or sale.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: Two of the storage chest freezers upstairs have damage to the interior of the lid, creating cracks and crevices. Repair the cooler lids so the surface is smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-202.16 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The chest freezers upstairs were observed to be soiled with mold around the sides of the lids and lid seals. PIC was informed that chest freezers are in need of a deep clean. Ensure chest freezers are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent mold accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The flooring in the upstairs dry storage area was observed to be in disrepair. The floors are cracked, bubbled, and wearing thin. This makes it difficult to properly clean the floors, posing the risk of cross-contamination. Ensure floors are repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The floors in the outdoor walk-in cooler were observed to be soiled with food debris. Ensure staff are cleaning floors of coolers often enough to avoid accumulation of food debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Raw shell eggs observed stored above thawing vegetables in the bottom of the short prep cooler. CORRECTED- Storage was rearranged to store vegetables above eggs. Ensure foods are stored to prevent potential cross contamination.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Six (1 gal) containers of cheese sauce, in the walk-in cooler and labeled indicating cooling began at 10am, were observed at 104-136F (probed). Four containers were observed at 104F to 109F, and were voluntarily discarded. Two containers, observed at 135F and 136F, were kept to be cooled. Upon returning to the kitchen, staff explained that they had mismarked the time cooling began. Ensure foods are cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours, and are cooled from 135F to 41F within 6 hours. Keep logs to show that foods are being cooled properly and that the process is being monitored. 
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. [C]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Thermometers were not found in several coolers on the cookline. Ensure ambient air thermometers are present in all cold holding units. CORRECTED- PIC found thermometers upstairs and added them to each of the cookline coolers.
4-204.112: (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
One of the storage chest freezers upstairs has damage to the interior of the lid, creating cracks and crevices. Repair the cooler lid so the surface is smooth and easily cleanable.
4-202.16: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
No measurable sanitizer concentration was observed at the dish machine after three full cycles were run. There appears to be damage to the sanitizer line. PIC reached out to GFS for maintenance. The three compartment sink will be used to wash, rinse, and sanitize dishes until the dish machine is repaired.
4-501.114: (A) Chlorine shall have minimum concentration (50-200ppm). [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
No measurable sanitizer concentration was observed in the kitchen sanitizer buckets. CORRECTED- PIC changed out the sanitizer concentrate jug, which was low. Sanitizer buckets were remade from the wall-mounted dispenser, and were observed at 400ppm quat.
4-501.114: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration based on label (200-400ppm). [P]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment: Thawed portions of vacuum-packaged fish were observed in the walk-in cooler with packaging intact. Ensure vacuum packaged portions of fish are properly thawed when product is available for sale at the facility. Labeling indicates the product should stay frozen until use and be removed from packaging to thaw under refrigeration. At minimum the packaging needs to be cut to eliminate reduced oxygen environment. Ensure packaging is cut from the moment vacuum packaged fish is taken from the freezer to begin thawing in the walk-in cooler.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13 Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in  (B) of this section. [C]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Thermometers were not found in several coolers on the cookline. Ensure ambient air thermometers are present in all cold holding units.
4-204.112: (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Food debris and soil accumulation were observed under and behind equipment on the cookline, and on the wall under the 3 compartment sink and dish machine. Clean physical facilities.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Kitchen dicer press and upstairs can opener blade observed soiled with food debris. Maintain food contact surfaces clean to sight and touch. CORRECTED- Both pieces of equipment were removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Handwashing signage was not posted at the bar handwashing sink. Ensure all handwashing sinks have appropriate signage posted indicating their purpose.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.14 A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
No sanitizer buckets present at time of inspection. Per PIC, staff dumped sanitizer buckets after the lunch rush, and apparently forgot to replenish them. CORRECTED- PIC made sanitizer buckets to 400ppm quat.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration of 200-400ppm. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
Two (approx 1 gal each) containers of cheese sauce observed in the walk in cooler at 80F (probed). All three containers were without time stamps. Per PIC, cheese was placed in the walk-in cooler at 11:30pm. Containers had been in the walk-in cooler for 2.5 hours at the time of inspection. Ice baths were used to speed the cooling process. At 3:30pm, inspector checked temperatures again. Both containers were observed to be 75F (probed). CORRECTED- Cheese sauce was voluntarily discarded. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling. Ensure containers are labeled with time stamps when the cooling process began.
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 1) Floor and attached plumbing at the bar were soiled with general buildup at the north corner to the right of the ice bin. Detail cleaning was discussed. Ensure the crevices where bottle caps can accumulate and plumbing under the sinks are also getting cleaned as needed.
2) Floor along walls under ice machine were soiled with buildup of single service articles and general debris. Detail cleaning was discussed as well as the need for potential repairs along the floor to wall juncture.  
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the bar handwashing sink or in the men’s restroom. Signs were provided and posted during inspection.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Several of the soda nozzle diffusers at the south server station were soiled with chunky buildup. GM noted the nozzles are getting soaked nightly but was unsure as to how often they are scrubbed for cleaning. Nozzles and diffusers were removed for cleaning. Ensure proper cleaning and sanitizing of soda nozzles and diffusers.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Cheese sauce made during morning prep was in the walk-in cooler in eight containers (~1gal each) in the process of cooling. Four containers with a time stamp or 10:30am had internal temperatures at 36F, 47F, 48F, and 49.5F. Four other containers that were warm to the touch and without time stamps had internal temperatures at 122F, 125F, 126F, and 130F. Based on information provided to the GM by the cook the warmer portions were prepared around 11:30-11:45am. Time and temperature were not being monitored to verify product was reaching benchmark temperature of 70F within the first 2hrs, and product was in the cooler for over 3hrs at the time of inspection based on information provided. Cheese sauce at 122F-130F was reheated to begin cooling process again. Cooling was discussed at length with GM. Ensure foods are cooling quickly and properly.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.citation_text:
3-501.19 Pan of leaf lettuce was observed on top of the reach-in cooler. Lettuce was at 72F, and container did not have a time stamp as required by the time control policy established during the previous routine inspection. Lettuce was discarded. Ensure working supplies of lettuce held at room temperature during lunch service are labeled with a time stamp and used or discarded within 4hrs.
If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours, food shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time frame for use and cannot exceed 4 hours. The food must be served or discarded within 4 hours. The food in unmarked containers or packages, or marked to exceed a 4-hour limit shall be discarded

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Thawed portions of vacuum packaged fish were observed in the walk-in cooler with packaging intact. Fish in question is only available during Lent season. Ensure vacuum packaged portions of fish are properly thawed when product is available for sale at the facility. Labeling indicates the product should stay frozen until use and be removed from packaging to thaw under refrigeration. At minimum the packaging needs to be cut to eliminate reduced oxygen environment. Ensure packaging is cut from the moment vacuum packaged fish is taken from the freezer to begin thawing in the walk-in cooler. 
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in ¶(A) of this section; or prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in ¶ (B) of this section.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 Box of French fries was observed on the floor under the kitchen handwashing sink. It was unclear as to why the fries were under the handwashing sink. Box was discarded and fries were placed back in the walk-in cooler. 
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food in a clean, dry location; where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 The following ares were observed to be soiled:
1. Floor and walls under and around equipment in the kitchen (general buildup);
2. Walls and attached plumbing under kitchen 3 part sink (grimy buildup);  and
3. Floor in dry storage at bulk flour and spice storage (powder accumulation). 
Cleaning frequency and upcoming detail cleaning were discussed. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Flatbreads were observed unwrapped and sitting directly on the shelf in the bottom holding area of the pizza prep cooler. Manager noted that is not the normal practice for storage and flatbreads are typically stored in plastic wrap. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Dish machine final rinse chlorine concentration was observed at ~10-25ppm. Sanitizer jug was almost empty. After providing a new jug of sanitizer and priming the chemical line the final rinse concentration was observed below 50ppm. A call for service was made during inspection, and management was informed a technician would be able to come out for service on Thursday of this week. The kitchen 3 part sink was setup during inspection (200ppm quat). In the meantime, the kitchen manager ran the dish machine for another half dozen plus cycles, and the final rinse concentration reach 50ppm. It would appear the lower concentration during previous cycles was due to old chemical, which worked its way through the tubing after priming and running multiple cycles. 
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions (no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm). Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Three 5gal containers of cheese sauce in the walk-in cooler were observed with surface temperatures of 50F-55F and internal temperatures of 77F-79F. The label on containers had a prep time of 12pm, and temperatures were checked by inspector at ~3:20pm. Based on labeling alone the cheese sauce did not cool to 70F/below within 2hrs. Cheese sauce was reheated to begin cooling process again. 
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Containers of leaf lettuce and sliced tomato were observed on top of a reach-in cooler where toppings are held during lunch service. Lettuce was observed at 72F and was discarded. Sliced tomato had an internal temperature of 53F and was removed from cold holding recently. Tomato was placed in the reach-in cooler. Staff regularly have leaf lettuce, sliced tomato, pickles, carrots, celery, and onion out for quick assembly during lunch service. A time control policy was established for leaf lettuce and sliced tomato. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Chemical bottle of a pink colored liquid was observed unlabeled at the bar. Management was unsure as to what was in the bottle. The product was discarded during inspection.
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 1. Wire shelving units in the kitchen and dish area were soiled with general buildup.
2. Counter under heating/hot holding units was soiled with buildup of food debris.
3. General outer surfaces of panini presses and trays underneath were soiled with food debris. 
4. Buildup of food crumbs was observed in the reach-in freezer under the pizza ovens.
5. General buildup of food crumbs and splash were observed inside the bottom holding area of the pizza prep cooler.
6. General surfaces of dish machine were soiled with buildup.
7. Sides of cooking equipment and coolers were soiled with grease and general buildup. 
Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Floor under cooking equipment and walls behind and around equipment were soiled with general buildup and debris. Cleaning frequency and upcoming detail cleaning were discussed. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Cook exited the building to retrieve food from the walkin cooler. Upon re-entering the kitchen hands were not washed prior to putting on gloves to continue with food prep. Handwashing between tasks, upon entering the kitchen, and prior to putting on gloves were discussed.  
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, prior to putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed and observed being used for remainder of inspection.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Portions of cooled cheese sauce said to be prepared the day prior were uncovered in the walkin cooler. PIC was advised on covering foods once items are properly cooled. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Portions of deli meats in top of sandwich/salad prep cooler were without date marks. Portions were said to be from a container that was date marked in the walkin cooler. The container in the walkin cooler was also without a date mark. Portions of bagged lettuce and cooled cheese sauce were also missing date marks in the walkin cooler. Lettuce and deli meats were portioned earlier today, and cheese sauce was said to be from the previous operating day. Date marks were added to foods based on information provided. Ensure proper date marking of prepared foods and proper discard within 7 days. 
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Cheese sauce was observed cooling in a covered 18qt container in the walkin cooler. The container was approximately half full and observed with surface and internal temperatures at 81F and 120F respectively. Cook who prepared the cheese sauce left around 2:15pm, and cheese sauce prep was the last thing the cook did prior to leaving based on information provided. Time and temperature were not being monitored for cooling cheese sauce. PIC put the container of cheese sauce in an ice bath and added an ice wand to the product to aid in rapid cooling. Ensure proper and rapid chilling of cooling TCS foods.  
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.  When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be: (1) Arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls; and (2) Loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination as specified under Subparagraph 3-305.11(A)(2), during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15 The back door was observed to be slightly ajar and not closed flush with the door frame. The door is not self-closing and is not tight fitting unless pulled shut. As of the previous inspection, the bottom hinge wasn't working properly. Provide repairs to the back door so it is self closing and tight fitting.  
Outer openings of a food establishment shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit was not available for use. Obtain and use quat test strips to verify concentration of sanitizer solutions prepared at the wall mounted dispenser and at the bar 3 part sink for ware washing (see general comments for additional information).
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions in mg/L shall be provided. Obtain and use quat test strips with sanitizer used on food contact surfaces in the kitchen.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not available for use in the kitchen. Cook noted the sani-buckets were just emptied after lunch rush. PIC was advised sani-buckets need to be setup and available for use during all hours of prep and operation. When used sanitizer is discarded, ensure that fresh solution is provided for use.
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.
